terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, founder of VKontakte, subject of the biography
terms.why_hard: Name transliteration differs across languages and must stay consistent book-wide

terms.gloss: A classmate/interlocutor of Durov's (apparently a school friend recounting these episodes)
terms.why_hard: Minor character whose identity and role must be researched and name form fixed for later appearances

terms.gloss: to lecture in a preachy, mentor-like tone; the author's ironic verb for Durov's didactic monologues
terms.why_hard: Authorial sarcasm; a neutral 'continued' loses the mocking tone

terms.gloss: First half of the proverb 'работа не волк, в лес не убежит' — work won't run away into the forest
terms.why_hard: Russian-only pun on 'волк/лес'; needs an explicit or substituted idiom for laziness

proposed.en: 'work isn't a wolf — it won't run off into the woods'
proposed.zh: “工作又不是狼，不会跑进树林里”（俄谚，意为工作跑不掉）
proposed.ja: 「仕事は狼ではない、森へ逃げない」（＝仕事は待っていてくれるというロシアの諺）

terms.gloss: Ivan Goncharov, 19th-century Russian novelist, author of Oblomov
terms.why_hard: Needs the Oblomov link to be clear to readers without Russian literary schooling

terms.gloss: The famously lazy gentry hero of Goncharov's 1859 novel; archetype of inertia
terms.why_hard: In Russian the name alone means 'lazy person'; other readers need a minimal gloss

proposed.en: 'the lovable Oblomov' (with brief apposition: Goncharov's famously idle hero)
proposed.zh: 可爱的奥勃洛莫夫（冈察洛夫笔下著名的懒人典型）
proposed.ja: 愛すべきオブローモフ（ゴンチャロフ笔下の怠惰の象徴）

terms.gloss: Andrei Stolz, the energetic, methodical German-Russian foil to Oblomov
terms.why_hard: Durov's word 'механистичный' (mechanical) frames him; rendering must keep the Oblomov/Stolz opposition

terms.gloss: Literary-critical term for a character who moralises at length; here a half-ironic label for Durov
terms.why_hard: Untranslatable critical jargon; 'lecturer' or 'windbag' both distort it

proposed.ja: 持論を垂れる評論家ぶり

terms.gloss: Colloquial 'he rips into everyone / badmouths everyone' (гнать на кого-то = to trash-talk)
terms.why_hard: Slang verb; literal 'drives against' is nonsense in English

proposed.ja: 誰彼かまらずこき下ろす

terms.gloss: Fyodor Dostoevsky, whom Durov called 'a terrible writer'
terms.why_hard: The shock of the judgement depends on name recognition; keep the canonical form

terms.gloss: Chekhov's last play (1904) about a gentry estate's cherry orchard sold at auction
terms.why_hard: Chinese/Japanese titles vary (樱花 vs 樱桃园; 桜の園); must fix one book-wide

terms.gloss: The merchant in The Cherry Orchard who buys the estate and cuts down the orchard
terms.why_hard: Readers need to know he is the parvenu-merchant figure the 'intelligent children' despise

terms.gloss: Ranevskaya, the impoverished aristocratic owner of the orchard in the play
terms.why_hard: The 'lacy soul' metaphor only works if she is recognisably the refined gentry figure

terms.gloss: Allusion to Tyutchev's line 'нельзя понять Россию умом' family of imagery — a booted intruder trampling a lace soul
terms.why_hard: Echoes the famous 'юродивый в лаптях' / cultured-vs-merchant trope; must stay vivid, not flattened

proposed.en: who stomped his boots into Ranevskaya's lacy soul
proposed.zh: 穿着长靴闯进朗涅夫斯卡娅蕾丝般精致心灵的人
proposed.ja: 長靴でラネーフスカヤのレースのような魂に踏み込んだ

terms.gloss: 'A man of action/deeds', a stock Russian positive epithet opposed to the dreamy intelligentsia
terms.why_hard: Set phrase with Soviet-era resonance; 'practical man' undersells the ideological weight

terms.gloss: 'Our wondrous country' — ironico-affectionate stock phrase for Russia
terms.why_hard: Irony of 'чудный' (marvellous/absurd) must survive; 'wonderful' is too flat

terms.gloss: stayed overnight at someone's place (crashed there), a common youth/traveler term
terms.why_hard: A careless translator might render it as 'registered' or 'signed up' from the root 'писать'; it means 'crashed at / stayed over'

terms.gloss: Bolshaya Morskaya Street, a major street in central St Petersburg running toward Palace Square
terms.why_hard: Must be rendered consistently throughout the book; transliteration vs. translation ('Great Maritime') is the key decision

proposed.ja: ボルシャヤ・モルスカヤ通り

terms.gloss: Palace Square, the central square of St Petersburg in front of the Winter Palace
terms.why_hard: Well-known landmark; must be consistent with any other mentions in the book

terms.gloss: people bundled up against the cold like they're in cases/shells; echoes Chekhov's 'Man in a Case'
terms.why_hard: A careless translator might miss the Chekhov allusion and just say 'bundled-up people'; the literary echo matters for tone

terms.term: Двери в трамвае стреляли, как красные матросы
terms.gloss: tram doors slammed/banged like Red sailors (Bolshevik sailors) firing guns; a humorous simile evoking revolutionary imagery
terms.why_hard: A careless translator might lose the humor or the specific historical allusion to revolutionary sailors; needs to convey both sound and the cheeky comparison

proposed.en: The tram doors fired off like Red sailors
proposed.zh: 电车门砰砰作响，像红色水兵在开炮
proposed.ja: トラムのドアは赤軍の水兵のように撃ち放たれた

terms.gloss: one of the Rostral Columns on Vasilievsky Island, St Petersburg; a landmark with an interior space
terms.why_hard: Must be consistent; a translator unfamiliar with St Petersburg might not know these are specific monuments, not generic columns

terms.gloss: archways/gateways passing through buildings into courtyards, a defining feature of St Petersburg urban fabric
terms.why_hard: Not just 'alley' or 'gate'; these are the characteristic pass-through arches of Petersburg apartment blocks, and the word recurs in Petersburg literature

terms.gloss: glacial moraines; snowdrifts compared to geological deposits left by a glacier creeping over the cobblestones
terms.why_hard: The metaphor is extended and geological; a careless translator might flatten it to 'huge snowdrifts'

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, the subject of the biography
terms.why_hard: Must be consistently rendered across the entire book; in some contexts it refers to Pavel, in others possibly to his brother Nikolai

terms.gloss: a handrail on the metro station escalator or platform edge; here it means the crowd flow pushes you toward the railing
terms.why_hard: In context it refers to the specific dangerous spot in a metro crowd where you get pressed against the handrail; not just any railing

terms.gloss: copper coins, small change; colloquial term for low-denomination coins
terms.why_hard: A careless translator might say 'medals' or 'copper ingots'; it means small coins, specifically kopecks

terms.term: третья строчка снизу яснее не стала
terms.gloss: a self-referential aside meaning 'the third line from the bottom hasn't become any clearer' — a meta-comment on his handwriting or the text itself
terms.why_hard: This is a playful authorial aside that breaks the fourth wall; a careless translator might treat it as a literal description of a notebook

proposed.en: the third line from the bottom is no clearer for it
proposed.zh: 倒数第三行依然看不清楚
proposed.ja: 下から三行目は相変わらず読みにくいが

terms.gloss: occupied (a desk), used humorously/militarily to mean he took over the front desk
terms.why_hard: Deliberately military vocabulary applied to a schoolboy's seat choice; tone must be preserved

terms.gloss: hunched over; describes Durov's posture at his desk, a recurring physical detail
terms.why_hard: This is a recurring characterization of Durov's body language and should be rendered consistently each time it appears

terms.gloss: scratched/scrawled on the blackboard; 'нацарапано' implies crude, scratched writing rather than neat chalk writing
terms.why_hard: The verb choice (нацарапано, not написано) implies roughness; a careless translator would just say 'written on the board'

terms.gloss: wind tunnels; the author compares the archways (подворотни) to wind tunnels because of the funneling effect of wind through them
terms.why_hard: A technical metaphor applied to urban architecture; must be kept vivid and not flattened to 'windy passages'

terms.term: систему каналов, в которых бежит чужая жизнь
terms.gloss: The network of channels through which other people's lives flow; describes VKontakte as infrastructure carrying human experience.
terms.why_hard: Literal 'channels' might suggest plumbing or TV channels; it's a metaphor for data/social feeds and communication lines.

proposed.en: a system of channels through which other people's lives flow
proposed.zh: 承载着他人生活奔流的渠道系统
proposed.ja: 他人の人生が流れるチャンネル網

terms.gloss: Homunculus-identities; artificial, miniature human replicas created in a lab, here meaning fake or curated online personas.
terms.why_hard: The alchemical term 'homunculus' might be missed; it implies artificial creation and miniature scale, not just 'fake profiles'.

proposed.ja: ホムンクルス的アイデンティティ

terms.gloss: Pirates of Silicon Valley; 1999 TV movie about the early days of Apple and Microsoft, featuring Steve Jobs and Bill Gates.
terms.why_hard: Knowing the specific scene referenced (the director being told he's making a blockbuster, not a commercial) requires familiarity with the film.

proposed.ja: パイレーツ・オブ・シリコンバレー

terms.gloss: Steve Jobs; co-founder of Apple Inc., depicted in the film Pirates of Silicon Valley.
terms.why_hard: Standard rendering is needed across languages to maintain the connection to the tech industry narrative.

terms.gloss: A potent/powerful salesman of ideas; describes Durov's persuasive charisma and reality distortion field.
terms.why_hard: 'Сильнодействующий' literally means 'strong-acting' (like a drug); implies powerful, possibly dangerous efficacy, not just 'good' salesmanship.

proposed.zh: 极具说服力的理念推销员
proposed.ja: 強力なアイデアのセールスマン

terms.gloss: VKontakte (VK); the Russian social networking service founded by Pavel Durov.
terms.why_hard: Whether to transliterate (VKontakte), translate (InTouch), or use the modern abbreviation (VK) affects consistency throughout the book.

terms.term: so long, and thanks for all the fish
terms.gloss: So Long, and Thanks for All the Fish; title of the fourth Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy book by Douglas Adams, used as a humorous farewell.
terms.why_hard: The abrupt switch to English and the literary allusion must be recognized as a citation, not a translation error.

proposed.en: so long, and thanks for all the fish
proposed.ja: さようなら、魚をありがとう

terms.gloss: Douglas Adams; British author of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy series.
terms.why_hard: Standard transliteration is required to identify the author correctly across all language versions.

terms.gloss: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy; the series title for Adams's science fiction comedy books.
terms.why_hard: The Russian title uses a prepositional case construction ('by hitchhiking across the galaxy'); English reverts to the original title.

proposed.en: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
proposed.ja: 銀河ヒッチハイク・ガイド

terms.gloss: Vogons; a fictional alien race in Adams's series who destroy Earth to make way for a hyperspace bypass.
terms.why_hard: Requires knowledge of the fictional species and their bureaucratic, destructive nature in the source material.

terms.gloss: Hyperspace express route/bypass; the reason given for Earth's demolition in the Adams novel.
terms.why_hard: The Russian 'экспресс-маршрут' (express route) corresponds to the original 'hyperspace bypass'; consistency with standard translations of the Adams novel is key.

proposed.ja: ハイパースペース・バイパス

terms.gloss: Saint Petersburg; the city where VKontakte was founded and where this scene is set.
terms.why_hard: The shortened form 'Петербург' vs. 'Санкт-Петербург' affects register; the windy, maritime climate reference is specific to the city's geography.

proposed.ja: サンクトペテルブルク

terms.gloss: A volume of Cervantes; refers to Don Quixote, establishing the protagonist as a reader of classic literature.
terms.why_hard: The specific book (likely Don Quixote) and the implication of intellectual pretension or romanticism might be lost.

terms.gloss: The entrance hall or stairwell of a Soviet-era apartment block; the common entryway shared by residents.
terms.why_hard: English lacks a direct equivalent for this specific architectural and social space; 'entrance' or 'lobby' may not convey the utilitarian Soviet reality.

terms.gloss: Deserted/empty city blocks; describes the sparse, windswept urban landscape of the specific St. Petersburg district.
terms.why_hard: The contrast between 'blocks' (urban) and 'fields' (rural/undeveloped) suggests a specific liminal zone in the city's geography.

terms.gloss: High-voltage transmission towers/pylons; industrial infrastructure marking the landscape.
terms.why_hard: The visual of these towers is characteristic of certain post-Soviet industrial or peripheral districts.

terms.gloss: Face; colloquial term (slightly humorous or crude) for the face, derived from 'physiognomy'.
terms.why_hard: Register is colloquial; using 'face' is fine, but 'physiognomy' in English sounds overly scientific or ironic, which may or may not fit the tone.

terms.gloss: The sea is nearby; refers to the Gulf of Finland, establishing the geographical setting of the scene.
terms.why_hard: The proximity to the sea explains the wind mentioned earlier; the specific body of water (Gulf of Finland/Baltic) may need clarification.

terms.gloss: Chapter 1; standard book section heading.
terms.why_hard: Whether to use numerals (Chapter 1) or spelled-out numbers (Chapter One) affects the book's stylistic consistency.

terms.gloss: Botanical Garden; the title of Chapter 1, likely referring to the specific neighborhood or the actual garden in St. Petersburg.
terms.why_hard: May refer to the specific Saint Petersburg Botanical Garden or a neighborhood named after it; capitalization and translation consistency matter.

terms.gloss: As they say; a filler phrase used to introduce a quotation or cliché.
terms.why_hard: The ironic or distancing tone when introducing a foreign-language quote must be preserved.

terms.gloss: The director from the first scene; refers to the character in the film who is making a commercial but is told he's making a blockbuster.
terms.why_hard: The specific role (director vs. producer) and the scene's context in the film need to be understood to convey the analogy to Durov's persuasiveness.

proposed.en: the director from the opening scene

terms.gloss: Scoundrel/rascal; a mild, somewhat old-fashioned or literary insult for the bad driver who parked poorly.
terms.why_hard: The tone is literary/humorous rather than genuinely angry; 'scoundrel' or 'jerk' captures it better than 'bastard'.

terms.gloss: Squeeze through; describes pedestrians barely fitting past the poorly parked car.
terms.why_hard: The physical imagery of tight urban spaces is specific to dense Russian city planning.

terms.gloss: Of Shakespearean intensity and Homeric scope.
terms.why_hard: The paired literary allusions must stay grand and balanced; a careless translator may weaken 'накала' or 'размаха'.

proposed.en: of Shakespearean intensity and Homeric scope
proposed.zh: 莎士比亚式的烈度与荷马式的恢弘
proposed.ja: シェイクスピア的な激しさとホメロス的なスケール

terms.term: буквально-таки валяются под ногами, да некому подобрать
terms.gloss: Literally lie around underfoot with no one to pick them up — stories going to waste.
terms.why_hard: The colloquial intensifier 'буквально-таки' and elliptical second clause can sound unnatural if translated literally.

proposed.en: are literally lying around underfoot, and there is no one to pick them up
proposed.zh: 简直就散落在脚边，却没人去捡拾
proposed.ja: 文字どおり足元に転がっているのに、拾い上げる者がいない

terms.term: люди без имени и, в общем, без судьбы
terms.gloss: People without a name and, by and large, without a destiny — anonymous nobodies.
terms.why_hard: The hedging 'в общем' and literary 'без судьбы' are easy to flatten into 'ordinary people'.

proposed.en: people without a name and, by and large, without a destiny
proposed.zh: 没有名字、大体上也没有命运的人
proposed.ja: 名もなく、おおむね運命も持たない人々

terms.gloss: Masters of the universe.
terms.why_hard: The absolute-power metaphor must be rendered with equivalent grandiosity in each language.

terms.gloss: Cast down into the dirt — disgraced or humiliated.
terms.why_hard: Passive construction plus 'грязь' must convey sudden fall from power, not literal dirt-throwing.

terms.gloss: Cosmic mad whirl; 'свистопляска' is a folksy word for chaotic commotion.
terms.why_hard: The colloquial noun has no direct equivalent and must keep a vivid, slightly ironic register.

proposed.ja: 宇宙的などんちゃん騒ぎ

terms.term: не отливается не то что в граните – а даже в книжках в мягкой обложке
terms.gloss: Is not cast even in granite, let alone in paperback books — not immortalized in any durable form.
terms.why_hard: The 'не то что... а даже' construction reverses typical English 'let alone' logic; translators often flip the emphasis.

proposed.en: is not cast in granite, or even in paperback books
proposed.zh: 别说浇铸成花岗岩，就连平装书里都没有凝固下来
proposed.ja: 花崗岩どころか、ペーパーバックにさえ鋳込まれない

terms.gloss: PR operatives or spin doctors cover their tracks.
terms.why_hard: 'Пиарщик' is a mildly pejorative period colloquialism, and 'путают следы' is an idiom for obfuscation.

proposed.ja: PR屋が足跡を混乱させる

terms.term: «реальность настолько неустойчива и неоформленна, что ускользает от любого описания»
terms.gloss: A fashionable cliché: reality is so unstable and unformed that it eludes any description.
terms.why_hard: Must keep quotation marks and the deliberately vague intellectual register, possibly reading as parody.

proposed.en: "reality is so unstable and unformed that it slips away from any description"
proposed.zh: “现实如此不稳定、未成形，任何描述都无法捕捉它”
proposed.ja: 「現実はあまりに不安定で形を成しておらず、いかなる記述からもすり抜ける」

terms.gloss: A rotten excuse or cop-out.
terms.why_hard: 'Отмазка' is slang for a flimsy excuse and 'гнилая' intensifies contempt; register must stay informal.

terms.gloss: Kommersant, a leading Russian business daily.
terms.why_hard: Proper name must be transliterated consistently and recognized as a newspaper, not a generic 'merchant'.

terms.gloss: Vedomosti, a Russian business daily.
terms.why_hard: Proper name must be transliterated consistently and not confused with the historical Vedomosti.

terms.gloss: Social networks or social media.
terms.why_hard: Russian abbreviation; target languages must choose the natural period term consistently.

terms.gloss: Servers in California, standing for Silicon Valley-based internet companies.
terms.why_hard: Metonym must preserve geographic specificity rather than collapsing into 'American servers'.

proposed.ja: カリフォルニアのサーバー

terms.gloss: The pages of Kommersant.
terms.why_hard: Adjectival form must keep a visible link to the already translated proper name 'Kommersant'.

terms.gloss: Silicon Valley.
terms.why_hard: Russian calque 'Кремниевая долина' should become the standard target term and stay tied to the California-server contrast.

terms.gloss: Registered or domiciled, of servers or domain names; evokes the Soviet propiska residence permit.
terms.why_hard: The metaphor is legal-residential, not merely 'located'; translators often flatten it to 'hosted'.

terms.gloss: Jack Dorsey, co-founder of Twitter
terms.why_hard: A careless translator might not recognize the shortened Russian surname as Dorsey and could transliterate it awkwardly

terms.gloss: Mark Zuckerberg, founder of Facebook
terms.why_hard: Must be rendered consistently throughout the book; different transliteration traditions exist

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, founder of VKontakte and subject of the biography
terms.why_hard: Central figure; must be consistent across all segments; some languages may prefer full name on first mention in a chapter

terms.gloss: Brad Fitzpatrick, creator of LiveJournal
terms.why_hard: The genitive case and Russian transliteration could confuse; the text identifies him by his creation, so the translator must decide how much context to give

proposed.ja: ブラッド・フィッツパトリック

terms.gloss: LiveJournal, the blogging platform hugely popular in Russia in the 2000s, founded by Brad Fitzpatrick
terms.why_hard: In Russian internet culture LJ (ЖЖ) was far more culturally significant than in the English-speaking world; the translator must decide whether to convey that weight

terms.gloss: Facebook, the social network
terms.why_hard: Straightforward but must be consistent with how the book handles the name elsewhere

terms.gloss: Twitter, the microblogging platform
terms.why_hard: Must be consistent; the text uses it as a metonym for a type of media function (news agency field)

terms.gloss: One-directional connections, i.e. the follow/subscribe model as opposed to mutual friendship
terms.why_hard: A literal translation ('one-sided links') might not convey the specific social-media feature; must match the term used elsewhere in the book for this concept

terms.gloss: The feature that pulls/attaches a preview image to a shared link (like Facebook's link preview thumbnails)
terms.why_hard: The verb подсасывание is colloquial/slangy (literally 'sucking in'); a careless translator might render it too literally or too formally, losing the informal tone

proposed.en: pulling a nice image into a link
proposed.zh: 为链接自动抓取一张漂亮的配图
proposed.ja: リンクにきれいな画像を引っ張ってくる機能

terms.gloss: The news feed (лента = feed/timeline in social media context)
terms.why_hard: In Russian social-media slang лента specifically means the news feed; a literal 'ribbon' or 'tape' would be wrong

terms.gloss: Topical/urgent issues of the day, hot-button current affairs
terms.why_hard: The word carries a slightly negative connotation of tedious daily politics; a neutral rendering loses Durov's irritation

terms.gloss: Programmers/developers, informal borrowing from English 'coders'
terms.why_hard: Must match the register used elsewhere in the book for this word; overly formal rendering would break the voice

terms.gloss: Subscribers/followers — users who follow someone without mutual friendship approval
terms.why_hard: Must be consistent with how the book renders the VK concept of подписчики vs. друзья; the distinction is central to this passage

terms.gloss: To irradiate/broadcast one's ideas to the audience — облучать literally means to irradiate, used here as an intense metaphor for broadcasting
terms.why_hard: A literal 'irradiate' sounds odd in English; the translator must find an equally vivid but natural equivalent that preserves Durov's intensity

proposed.en: bombard the audience with his ideas
proposed.zh: 向用户灌输自己的想法
proposed.ja: 自分のアイデアをオーディエンスに浴びせる

terms.gloss: Privacy settings
terms.why_hard: Must be consistent with how this UI concept is rendered throughout the book

terms.gloss: A personalized newspaper — the metaphor for what Facebook was becoming
terms.why_hard: The newspaper metaphor is deliberate and contrasts with поле информагентства; both halves of the contrast must be rendered with parallel imagery

proposed.ja: パーソナライズされた新聞

terms.gloss: Ilya Shcheglov-Streshinsky, VK investor and associate of Usmarov's Mail.ru group
terms.why_hard: Transliteration varies (Streshinsky/Shcheglov-Streshinsky); must match other segments and reader needs to know which figure this is

terms.gloss: Alisher Usmanov, billionaire investor whose Mail.ru group held a large VK stake; the author's 'manager' is ironic, stressing the businessman-investor mindset
terms.why_hard: The epithet 'менеджер' is deliberately belittling; rendering it neutrally as 'businessman Usmanov' loses the sneer

proposed.ja: マネージャーとしてのウスマノフ

terms.gloss: VKontakte ('In Contact'), Russia's largest social network, founded by Durov
terms.why_hard: Book uses both 'ВКонтакте' and 'VK' in places; must pick one consistent form (VKontakte) and stick to it

terms.gloss: The American social network, framed here as VK's 'enemy' platform
terms.why_hard: The irony 'враждебный Facebook' plus the aside about Usmanov's early Facebook stake must survive

terms.gloss: The 'power vertical', Putin-era term for top-down centralized state authority
terms.why_hard: A fixed Russian political idiom; literal 'vertical of power' is opaque without the political connotation

proposed.zh: 实行权力垂直（自上而下集权）的国家
proposed.ja: 権力の垂直システム（トップダウン集権国家）

terms.gloss: Verkhovsky-like jest: 'The nerds have seized the noosphere' — Vernadsky's noosphere concept fused with geek culture
terms.why_hard: Ноосфера (Vernadsky's 'noosphere') is obscure abroad; the ironic grandiosity must be kept without a lecture

proposed.en: The nerds had taken over the noosphere
proposed.zh: 极客们占领了智慧圈（心智圈）
proposed.ja: オタクたちがノウアスフィアを制圧した

terms.gloss: Fixed biblical-flavored idiom: 'the powers that be / the great of this world'
terms.why_hard: Cliché must be rendered by an equivalent cliché, not literally

terms.gloss: Medieval-alchemy image for how Usmanov's circle imagined VK's programmers: sorcerers brewing a potion
terms.why_hard: Sustained medieval metaphor ('Средневековье в уме') that must stay coherent across the sentence

proposed.en: accursed sorcerers sitting there brewing their potion
